clue.text: Change direction about food, say, backing something meat-free

indicators.note: about means going around, so the direction change wraps itself round what follows

parts.note: to veer is to change direction

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the food and the 'say' are read from the end

parts.note: grub is informal for food
'say' introduces an example, as e.g. does

explanation.surface: A diner changes course about their meal and comes out in support of something vegetarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals an example, the job e.g. does; 'backing' turns the food and example round before the direction change wraps them.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie burger is a patty made without any animal flesh, so it is literally a meatless item.

clue.text: Animal passion almost rising to ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the shortened word runs backwards
almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the passion word is cut

parts.note: love is a passion
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An animal's passion grows until it nearly reaches ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vole is a small rodent, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Blow up a game reserve

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game
a spare is something kept in reserve

explanation.surface: Someone is told to blow up a nature reserve for game animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game reserve' reads as one thing but splits in two. To go spare is British slang for losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions describe suddenly becoming furious and losing one's temper in an angry outburst.

clue.text: Only undergarment visible after fastening belt up

indicators.note: after says the fastening word comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: a button is a fastening
the one and only: one means only
a slip is an undergarment, here one that is showing

explanation.surface: Someone's slip is the only undergarment showing once their belt is fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt up' looks like part of the dressing scene, but it is British slang for be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To button one's lip is an idiom for keeping quiet, matching the slang order to stop talking.

clue.text: Chemicals are dropping down a toilet

indicators.note: dropping down means falling away, so the first letter of 'are' is lost

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the gents is a British name for a men's public lavatory

explanation.surface: Chemicals are being flushed away down a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagents are substances used in laboratory reactions, so they are a kind of laboratory chemical compound.

clue.text: Skip over some novel ideas

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of novel and the start of ideas

explanation.surface: A reader skips past some of the new ideas in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit a sound or passage, passing over it without dwelling there.

clue.text: Cease endless pressure or crack

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: to quit is to cease
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Stop the relentless pressure or something will give way.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack can be a witty remark or wisecrack, the same as a clever one-liner.

clue.text: Howl from girl over spilt tea

indicators.note: over in a down clue suggests turning upside down, so the girl's name runs upwards

parts.note: Lulu is a girl's name

indicators.note: spilt tea is scattered, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl howls after knocking over her cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to wail with a long high trilling cry, much like an animal's howl.

clue.text: Rock song originally separating two musical qualities

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so the kept letter sits between the two qualities

parts.note: pitch is one quality of a musical sound

indicators.note: originally points to where the word starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of song
tone is a second quality of a musical sound

explanation.surface: A rock song is described as falling between two musical qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music genre, but it is the definition: a kind of volcanic glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitchstone is a dull glassy volcanic rock, so it is a type of stone found in nature.

clue.text: Second scorer for West Ham's drunk

definitions.text: Second scorer for West Ham's drunk

parts.words: Second scorer for West Ham's drunk
parts.note: surface: the player who scored West Ham's second goal was drunk

parts.words: Second scorer for West Ham's drunk
parts.note: setter: the second composer named in East London rhyming slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A footballer who scored West Ham's second goal was drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: A scorer is a composer here. In Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in East London where West Ham play, 'Brahms and Liszt' means pissed, that is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming slang phrase for being intoxicated pairs two composers, and the Hungarian pianist is named second.

clue.text: Soldier in an attempt to win victory for England

parts.note: taken as written
GI is an American soldier
to court is to try to win someone's affections

explanation.surface: A soldier makes an attempt to secure an English victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier in' means the soldier goes inside 'an', not that a soldier is fighting in the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle where Henry V's English army defeated the French.

clue.text: What might display China's control over ministers

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the control word above the ministers word

parts.note: to corner a market is to control it
the cabinet is the body of senior ministers

explanation.surface: A question of China's power over a government's ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes China look like the country; it is china, the crockery. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner cabinet is a piece of furniture fitting in a room's angle, often with glass doors for showing crockery.

clue.text: Faultless record held by sailor regarding fish

indicators.note: held by means gripped by the surrounding words, so the record sits inside them

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
over can mean about or regarding, as in a row over money
an EP is an extended-play record
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A sailor's spotless record is held up in a matter concerning fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held by' straddles the record with words on both sides: the sailor-and-regarding pair before it, the fish after.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond criticism has no flaws anyone could blame them for, so they are blameless.

clue.text: Did hound rescue pet mistreated by duke?

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: Did a hound go after a rescue animal that a duke had treated badly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a dog in a story about pets, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to harass them relentlessly, which is to persecute; both are past tense here.

clue.text: Canine still loves the fancy collars

indicators.note: collars means grabs round the neck, so the rearranged word goes around the rest
fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
yet means still, as in yet more
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O, so two of them

explanation.surface: A dog still loves the fancy collars it wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog, which fits the collars, but it means the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The canine is the pointed tooth below the eye, also called by this name in the upper jaw.

clue.text: Failing, move treacherously from side to side

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flaw or shortcoming

definitions.text: move treacherously from side to side
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to desert one's country or party for the opposing camp

explanation.walkthrough: 'From side to side' suggests swaying, but it means switching from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a shortcoming and a verb for abandoning allegiance to join the enemy.

clue.text: Ornamentation adjusted for uniform twice

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters of the short word are moved about

parts.note: for is taken as written; U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
twice means the same pair is written a second time

explanation.surface: Decoration on a uniform has been altered, and done twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou is fussy frilly decoration, especially on dresses, so it is showy trimming.

clue.text: Upset tin full of fish

indicators.note: full of means holding something inside, so the tin wraps around the fish

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over a tin packed with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as knocking over the tin, but it is the definition: emotionally disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shaken is disturbed and rattled emotionally, which is what being upset means.

clue.text: Nuts topped fish dish every now and again

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: salmon is a fish

indicators.note: every now and again means only at intervals, so alternate letters are taken

parts.note: first and third letters of dish

explanation.surface: Nuts sprinkled over a fish dish from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Almonds are edible seeds of a tree in the plum family, commonly classed as nuts.

clue.text: Laundry instruction one's left in red lacy pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be sorted
one has left, so the letter for one departs from the next word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A care label sewn into some red lacy underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: One is I, which leaves IN as N. 'Pants' looks like underwear, but it is the anagram signal; in Britain pants also means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry-clean is a care label direction telling the owner to have the garment cleaned without water.

clue.text: Sort of rock Cartier fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made into something, so the brand name is reshaped

parts.note: taken as written; Cartier is a jewellery house

explanation.surface: A rock, as in a diamond, made by the jeweller Cartier.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock suggests a gemstone from a jeweller; geologists call a boulder moved by a glacier an erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratic is a boulder carried far from its origin by glacial ice, a recognised type of stone.

clue.text: It's partly imaginary, this obsession with ketamine?

parts.note: a complex is an obsession or fixation
ketamine is an anaesthetic, something that numbs

explanation.surface: A fixation on the drug ketamine is partly in the user's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Read NUMBER as numb-er: a thing that makes you numb, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics such a value has a real part and an imaginary part, so it is only partly imaginary.

clue.text: Finally, burn energy by turning on gas

parts.note: by as in multiplication, three by four, is the times sign X
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: turning means facing the other way, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the next word, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of burn

explanation.surface: In the end, energy is burned by switching on the gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a heavy noble gas found in tiny amounts in the air.

clue.text: At shed, perspiring, lifting trees

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means raising, so the word reads upwards
shed means cast off, so those two letters are dropped from the next word

parts.note: someone perspiring is sweaty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at a garden shed, sweating as they lift trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden building but is a verb: AT is cast off from SWEATY.
explanation.definitionFit: Yews are evergreen conifers often planted in churchyards, so they are a kind of tree.

clue.text: Can the first one in help in the kitchen?

parts.note: tin is the British word for a can
an opener is the first to go in, as an opening batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Can the first person to arrive lend a hand in the kitchen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb starting a question; it is the noun for a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin-opener is a hand tool cooks use to get into cans, so it is a kitchen aid.

clue.text: It's among the last components of an older explosive

definitions.text: It's among the last components of an older explosive

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the first word goes inside the selected letters
the last components of the next words are their final letters

parts.note: the final letters of an, older and explosive
taken as written; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A substance sits among the ingredients of an old-fashioned explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, or saltpetre, was a key ingredient of gunpowder, the traditional explosive mixture.

clue.text: Little bother

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small amount, as in a splash of milk
second meaning: a mild curse, as in 'drat it'

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'not much trouble', but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a small quantity and an old-fashioned exclamation of annoyance like drat.

clue.text: They're not fair only plugging trendy gelati

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so this word is pushed in between the others

parts.note: in means fashionable
just means only
gelati are Italian ice creams

explanation.surface: Fashionable ice creams are unfairly filling the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustices are wrongs or unfair acts, plural like the clue's They're.
